title: Feelings and character
summary: Words for what people feel and what they are like.

questions.clue: This is the warm, slightly sad longing you feel for a time in the past.
questions.note: Originally a medical diagnosis meaning acute homesickness, from Greek words for return and pain.

questions.clue: This is the unhappy feeling you get when somebody else has the thing you want.
questions.note: Strictly envy is wanting what another has, and jealousy is fearing to lose what you already have, but the two are used for each other constantly.

questions.clue: This word describes somebody who refuses to change their mind however good your argument is.
questions.note: Obstinate is the more formal word and carries the same meaning. Determined is the version you use when you approve.

questions.clue: This is a feeling of worry about something that has not happened yet and may never happen.
questions.note: Fear has an object in front of you. Anxiety is directed at the future, which is why it has nothing to resolve it.

questions.clue: This word describes somebody who believes they are far more important than they are.
questions.note: Confident is the neutral word. Arrogant and conceited both add the judgement that the confidence is not earned.

questions.clue: This is the ability to understand and share what another person is feeling.
questions.note: Sympathy is feeling for somebody. Empathy is feeling with them, which is the harder and more useful thing.

questions.clue: This word describes somebody who does a thing although they would rather not.
questions.note: Reluctant still does it. Unwilling can mean refusing outright, which is why the clue says they do it anyway.

questions.clue: This is the deep sorrow felt after somebody close to you has died.
questions.note: Grief is the feeling; mourning is how it is expressed; bereavement is the fact of the loss.

questions.clue: This is the strong wish to know or learn something, which makes children ask why.
questions.note: The adjective is curious, which also means strange, as in a curious noise.

questions.clue: This word describes somebody willing to give more of their time or money than they need to.
questions.note: The noun is generosity. The opposite is mean in British English and stingy in both.
